title: Donor Journey Choreographer
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: shifted-frame (probability 0.2)
Title: Donor Journey Choreographer
Thesis: Reframes Northeastern's advancement gap as a donor-experience problem: orchestrate every touchpoint so the donor never feels handed off.
Why this frame: Rather than an ops-team coordination lens, this views fragmentation through the donor's lived experience, letting real engagement-channel behavior drive the orchestration design.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Marcus Bell
  Role: Mid-level alumni donor (Khoury College '09, season-ticket holder, $1.2K lifetime giving)
  Context: Boston-based software engineering manager who feels genuine affection for Northeastern but is increasingly annoyed by uncoordinated outreach. In a single week he received an annual-fund email, a college-specific phonathon call, and an athletics text — each asking for a different gift with no awareness of the others.
  Emotional state: Warm toward the institution but fraying — beginning to read every Northeastern email as 'another ask' rather than a relationship.
  Pain points:
    - Three teams contact him in the same week with conflicting, redundant solicitations.
    - His preferred channel (email, not phone) is ignored; he keeps getting calls at dinner.
    - Nobody acknowledges he just gave to athletics two weeks ago before the annual fund asks again.
    - Moments he genuinely cares about (Khoury alumni research showcase) get buried under generic appeals.
  JTBD: When Northeastern reaches out, I want to feel like one institution that knows and remembers me, so I can stay engaged on my terms instead of feeling harvested.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Annual Fund Gift Officer (Priya): Owns broad-base solicitation cadence; needs to know when to hold a send because another team has priority.
  - College Development Director (Khoury, Dan): Runs college-specific campaigns; wants moment-of-interest triggers tied to academic engagement.
  - Athletics Engagement Manager (Tasha): Manages season-ticket and game-day asks; must avoid stacking onto recent gifts.
  - Advancement Operations / CRM Steward (Luis): Governs the shared donor record, channel-preference data, and suppression rules.
  - VP of Advancement (Executive sponsor): Cares about cross-team KPI alignment, donor retention, and lifetime value lift.

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: The moment Marcus receives a single, coherent, well-timed engagement — a Khoury research-showcase invitation that arrives by email the morning after he RSVPs to a campus event — while two redundant solicitation asks are silently suppressed behind the scenes.

USE CASES (12) - the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Touchpoint Conflict Detection
     Trigger: Three advancement teams independently queue outreach to the same donor within a rolling 7-day window.
     Flow: System ingests all queued sends across teams → cross-references against the unified donor timeline → flags overlapping or contradictory asks → surfaces a conflict card to each gift officer → presents a recommended resolution ranking by relevance and recency.
     AI role: Scores each queued touchpoint for relevance, recency overlap, and channel collision, then ranks which single ask should proceed.
     Outcome: Only the highest-relevance, lowest-fatigue ask is delivered; the others are deferred or merged, and each team sees why.
  2. Next-Best-Engagement Sequencing
     Trigger: A donor completes a touchpoint (opens, attends, gives, or ignores) and becomes eligible for the next interaction.
     Flow: System reads the donor's response signal → updates journey stage → consults the sequencing model → proposes the next-best engagement with channel and timing → routes to the owning team's queue with a confidence note.
     AI role: Predicts the next interaction most likely to deepen engagement without triggering fatigue, balancing stewardship and solicitation.
     Outcome: Each touchpoint feels like a natural continuation of a conversation rather than a cold restart.
  3. Channel Preference Honoring
     Trigger: A team selects a delivery channel that conflicts with the donor's stated or inferred preference.
     Flow: Officer drafts outreach → system checks declared preferences and inferred channel affinity → warns if the chosen channel is low-affinity → suggests the optimal channel → officer accepts or overrides with a logged reason.
     AI role: Predicts channel affinity from historical open, click, answer, and attendance behavior even when no explicit preference is set.
     Outcome: Marcus stops getting dinner-time phone calls; outreach lands on email where he actually engages.
  4. Solicitation Fatigue Guardrails
     Trigger: A donor's cumulative ask-volume in a rolling window approaches a fatigue threshold.
     Flow: System tallies solicitation-weighted touchpoints → computes a fatigue score → when score crosses amber/red, blocks or downgrades new solicitations to stewardship-only → notifies queued teams → auto-releases the guardrail once the window cools.
     AI role: Models the donor-specific fatigue curve and predicts the disengagement risk of an incremental ask.
     Outcome: Donors are protected from over-asking; long-term retention and trust are preserved over short-term campaign pressure.
  5. Cross-Team Handoff Smoothing
     Trigger: Primary relationship ownership shifts from one team to another (e.g., athletics to college major-gifts).
     Flow: Triggering event detected → system assembles a handoff brief (history, sentiment, preferences, open asks) → notifies receiving officer → logs acknowledgment → suppresses duplicate intro outreach from the new team.
     AI role: Generates a concise human-readable handoff summary from the full interaction record so context is never lost.
     Outcome: The donor experiences continuity; the receiving officer sounds informed instead of starting from zero.
  6. Moment-of-Interest Triggering
     Trigger: The donor exhibits a high-intent signal (RSVPs to an event, clicks a research story, updates LinkedIn role).
     Flow: Signal captured → mapped to a relevant program theme → matched against eligible engagement assets → most resonant touchpoint queued with priority → delivered within the receptivity window.
     AI role: Detects intent signals and matches them to the single most resonant institutional moment to reach for.
     Outcome: Marcus receives the Khoury showcase invite precisely when his interest is fresh, not a generic appeal weeks later.
  7. Donor Sentiment Tracking
     Trigger: Any donor interaction produces a sentiment-bearing signal (reply text, survey, call note, unsubscribe).
     Flow: Signal captured → sentiment inferred → rolling sentiment trend updated → trend shifts surfaced on officer dashboards → declining trends raise a care flag before churn.
     AI role: Infers sentiment from unstructured text and behavioral cues and tracks the trajectory over time.
     Outcome: Teams see cooling relationships early and respond with stewardship instead of another ask.
  8. Journey Stage Visualization
     Trigger: An officer opens a donor profile or the journey board.
     Flow: System loads the unified timeline → classifies the donor's current journey stage → renders a horizontal lifecycle ribbon → annotates recent and upcoming touchpoints → highlights stage-appropriate next actions.
     AI role: Classifies the donor's lifecycle stage and recommends stage-appropriate moves.
     Outcome: Every team works from a single, legible picture of where Marcus is in his relationship.
  9. Quiet-Period Stewardship Nudge
     Trigger: A donor has had no positive touchpoint for an extended window but remains engagement-healthy.
     Flow: Dormancy detected → system distinguishes intentional rest from neglect → proposes a no-ask stewardship gesture (impact note, milestone acknowledgment) → routes to owning team.
     AI role: Identifies relationship-warming opportunities that aren't solicitations, preserving goodwill.
     Outcome: Donors feel valued between campaigns, not only when money is needed.
  10. Conflict-Free Send Scheduling
     Trigger: A campaign batch is scheduled across overlapping audience segments.
     Flow: Batch submitted → system simulates per-donor delivery against all other scheduled sends → resolves collisions by relevance and timing → returns a deconflicted send plan → officer approves.
     AI role: Optimizes the send calendar at the individual-donor level to eliminate same-week stacking.
     Outcome: No donor ever receives three asks in one week again; campaigns ship clean.
  11. Optimal Timing Recommendation
     Trigger: A touchpoint is ready to send but timing is unset.
     Flow: Officer requests timing → system analyzes the donor's historical receptivity windows → recommends day-of-week and time → schedules within the window → measures lift post-send.
     AI role: Predicts the individual receptivity window from past engagement timing patterns.
     Outcome: Outreach arrives when Marcus is most likely to engage, raising response without raising volume.
  12. Outcome Attribution & Shared KPI Rollup
     Trigger: A gift, RSVP, or engagement conversion occurs.
     Flow: Conversion captured → attributed across contributing touchpoints regardless of owning team → credited to shared journey KPIs → rolled into a cross-team scorecard → surfaced to leadership.
     AI role: Performs multi-touch attribution so teams share credit for orchestrated journeys rather than competing for the last touch.
     Outcome: Teams are incentivized to collaborate; the donor experience improves because no one hoards the ask.

KEY SCREENS (9) - every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Donor Journey Timeline - purpose: Show every cross-team touchpoint as one continuous, legible relationship story.
     Primary element: A horizontal lifecycle ribbon with channel-coded touchpoint nodes, sentiment shading, and upcoming-action markers.
     Motion character: Smooth horizontal scroll with parallax depth on the active stage; nodes gently pulse when newly added.
  2. Engagement Conflict Alert - purpose: Surface same-window collisions and let officers resolve with one decision.
     Primary element: A conflict card stacking the competing asks side by side with relevance scores and a 'let this one through' selector.
     Motion character: Cards fan out on entry; suppressed asks slide down and dim with a soft settle.
  3. Channel Preference Center - purpose: Display declared and inferred channel affinities and let donors and officers manage them.
     Primary element: Affinity meters per channel (email / call / text / event / mail) with a confidence indicator.
     Motion character: Meters fill with an eased sweep; confidence dots shimmer on update.
  4. Next-Best-Action Card - purpose: Recommend the single best next engagement with channel, timing, and rationale.
     Primary element: A focused action card with a one-line AI rationale, channel chip, timing chip, and accept/adjust controls.
     Motion character: Card rises into focus with a subtle lift-and-shadow; accept triggers a satisfying check sweep.
  5. Fatigue Risk Gauge - purpose: Visualize a donor's cumulative ask-load against their personal fatigue threshold.
     Primary element: A radial gauge transitioning green→amber→red with the active suppression state labeled.
     Motion character: Needle eases to position; amber/red zones breathe slowly to signal caution.
  6. Sentiment Pulse View - purpose: Track sentiment trajectory and flag cooling relationships early.
     Primary element: A sparkline of rolling sentiment with care-flag markers at inflection points.
     Motion character: Line draws on left-to-right; care flags drop in with a gentle bounce.
  7. Cross-Team Handoff Log - purpose: Record ownership transitions with full context and acknowledgment.
     Primary element: A threaded handoff entry showing from-team, to-team, auto-generated brief, and acknowledgment status.
     Motion character: New handoffs thread in from the top; acknowledgment toggles a soft color confirm.
  8. Deconflicted Send Calendar - purpose: Show the orchestrated, per-donor-clean campaign schedule across all teams.
     Primary element: A week-grid heatmap of scheduled sends with collision warnings resolved to zero.
     Motion character: Collision cells flash and then resolve to calm green as the optimizer runs.
  9. Shared KPI Scorecard - purpose: Roll up multi-touch attribution into cross-team shared metrics for leadership.
     Primary element: A scorecard of journey-level KPIs (retention, engagement health, attributed yield) with team contribution bars.
     Motion character: Bars grow on load with staggered timing; KPI deltas count up numerically.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) - every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Conflict-Free Send Scheduling
     User action: An officer schedules a campaign batch or queues an individual touchpoint.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: All queued and scheduled touchpoints across teams, donor timelines, relevance tags, channel collisions.
     Output: A per-donor deconflicted send plan with suppressed/deferred items and resolution rationale.
     User benefit: No donor ever receives stacked, contradictory asks in one window — the core promise of the product.
  2. Channel Affinity Prediction
     User action: An officer selects or reviews a delivery channel for an outreach.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Historical opens, clicks, call answers, text replies, event attendance, declared preferences.
     Output: A ranked channel affinity profile with confidence scores and a recommended channel.
     User benefit: Outreach lands where the donor actually engages, raising response without raising volume.
  3. Fatigue Risk Scoring
     User action: Any new solicitation is queued for a donor.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Rolling solicitation-weighted touchpoint history, gift recency, prior fatigue responses.
     Output: A green/amber/red fatigue score with recommended suppression or downgrade action.
     User benefit: Protects long-term donor trust by preventing over-asking before churn signals appear.
  4. Sentiment Inference
     User action: A donor reply, survey, call note, or unsubscribe is captured.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Unstructured donor text, call notes, behavioral signals.
     Output: A sentiment classification with intensity and a rolling trajectory update.
     User benefit: Teams catch cooling relationships early and respond with care instead of another ask.
  5. Optimal Timing Recommendation
     User action: An officer prepares to send a ready touchpoint.
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Per-donor historical engagement timestamps by channel and outcome.
     Output: A recommended day-and-time window with expected receptivity lift.
     User benefit: Engagement arrives in the donor's receptive window, improving outcomes without extra outreach.
  6. Next-Best-Engagement Generator (Headline Aha)
     User action: A donor produces a response or intent signal that advances their journey.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Unified timeline, journey stage, sentiment, fatigue, channel affinity, available assets, conflict state.
     Output: The single best next engagement with channel, timing, suppression of redundant asks, and a one-line warm rationale.
     User benefit: Delivers the moment where redundant asks vanish and the most relevant one arrives perfectly timed — Marcus feels known.
  7. Handoff Brief Generation
     User action: Relationship ownership transitions between teams.
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Full interaction history, sentiment trend, preferences, open asks.
     Output: A concise human-readable handoff brief for the receiving officer.
     User benefit: Continuity is preserved; the donor never repeats their story to a new team.
  8. Institutional Context Retrieval
     User action: An officer needs program facts, gift policy, or event details for a touchpoint.
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: Northeastern advancement knowledge base, program descriptions, gift policies, event calendars.
     Output: Grounded factual snippets to populate accurate, on-brand outreach content.
     User benefit: Outreach is accurate and institution-aware, avoiding embarrassing errors that erode trust.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: Warm editorial humanism with quiet data confidence — soft paper-toned canvas, a single warm accent (Northeastern-adjacent deep red used sparingly), generous whitespace, narrative-led timelines over dense dashboards. Human-first, never CRM-cold.
  Hero treatment: A single horizontal donor-journey ribbon dominates the hero, rendered as a flowing path of channel-coded nodes that visibly 'breathe' — the moment of suppression is shown as two asks gracefully fading away while one warm invite glows and advances. The hero communicates the entire thesis in one glance: one coherent story, not three competing ones.
  Motion character: Calm, eased, intentional. Nothing snaps harshly; transitions feel like a held conversation. Suppressions slide and dim gently rather than vanishing abruptly. Gauges breathe rather than blink. Approvals reward with a single satisfying sweep. Motion always reduces anxiety, never adds urgency.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these - the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. A warm, softly-lit portrait of a mid-career alumnus reading an email on a phone with a faint relieved smile, muted paper-toned palette, editorial photography style.
    2. An abstract illustration of three converging message paths merging into one glowing line, warm deep-red accent on cream, minimal and elegant.
    3. A serene campus showcase scene with diverse alumni and students examining research posters, golden-hour warmth, documentary feel.
    4. A subtle textured background of overlapping translucent timeline ribbons in soft warm neutrals, suitable as a hero canvas.
    5. An iconographic set of channel symbols (envelope, phone, speech bubble, calendar, letter) rendered in a consistent warm line-art style.
    6. A quiet illustration of a single warm lantern lighting a path while two others dim, metaphor for honored versus suppressed asks.

FEATURE ROADMAP (3 phases) - the prototype demonstrates Phase 1 in working code; later phases appear as roadmap surfaces inside the experience:
  1. Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3) - Unified Journey Foundations
     • Unified donor timeline ingesting touchpoints from all teams into one record.
     • Donor Journey Timeline screen with lifecycle ribbon and channel-coded nodes.
     • Channel Preference Center capturing declared preferences.
     • Touchpoint Conflict Detection with same-window collision flagging.
     • Engagement Conflict Alert card with manual let-through resolution.
     • Seeded dataset of 28 donors and 30 touchpoints for demo realism.
     Success: 100% of demo donors render a single coherent timeline; conflicts detected within 7-day window with zero false negatives in seed data.
  2. Phase 2 (Month 2) - Intelligence & Orchestration
     • Channel Affinity Prediction with confidence scoring.
     • Fatigue Risk Scoring with green/amber/red guardrails and auto-suppression.
     • Next-Best-Engagement Generator powering the headline aha moment.
     • Optimal Timing Recommendation per donor.
     • Sentiment Inference and Sentiment Pulse View.
     • Conflict-Free Send Scheduling with deconflicted calendar.
     • Multi-provider AI fallback (Gemini primary, Claude for copy, graceful degradation).
     Success: ≥80% of redundant asks auto-suppressed in seed scenarios; next-best-action recommendations carry a human-readable rationale 100% of the time.
  3. Phase 3 (Quarter 2) - Cross-Team Alignment & Scale
     • Cross-Team Handoff Smoothing with AI-generated handoff briefs.
     • Shared KPI Scorecard with multi-touch attribution rollup.
     • Quiet-Period Stewardship Nudge engine.
     • Moment-of-Interest Triggering from intent signals.
     • Officer override logging and governance audit trail.
     • Institutional Context Retrieval via Wiki RAG for accurate outreach copy.
     • Leadership analytics on retention and engagement-health lift.
     Success: Cross-team conflict count per donor reduced to near-zero; shared KPI scorecard adopted by all participating teams with attribution credited across journeys.

NARRATIVE ARC (6 beats) - the multi-timeframe user journey the prototype must SUGGEST through copy, seed data, and roadmap surfaces:
  1. Minute 1
     User: Officer Priya opens Marcus's journey and instantly sees one coherent timeline instead of scattered team records.
     AI: System has already unified touchpoints and classified Marcus's stage as 'engage'.
     Feeling: Relief — finally a single picture of the donor.
  2. Hour 1
     User: Priya queues an annual-fund ask and immediately sees a conflict alert: two other teams are also reaching out this week.
     AI: Conflict detection scores all three asks and recommends letting only the Khoury invite through.
     Feeling: Surprise then trust — the tool is protecting the donor for her.
  3. Day 1
     User: Marcus RSVPs to a campus event; that evening he receives one well-timed Khoury research-showcase email — and nothing else.
     AI: Next-Best-Engagement generator fires, suppresses two redundant asks, and times the invite to his receptivity window.
     Feeling: Marcus feels seen — 'they actually know me.'
  4. Week 1
     User: Teams review the deconflicted send calendar and see zero same-week stacking across the whole donor base.
     AI: Conflict-free scheduling has resolved collisions per-donor across all queued campaigns.
     Feeling: Collective calm — competition gives way to coordination.
  5. Month 1
     User: Marcus, no longer fatigued, opens emails again and makes an unsolicited gift to Khoury research.
     AI: Fatigue guardrails kept asks low; sentiment trend reverses from cooling to rising.
     Feeling: Marcus feels like a valued partner, not a target.
  6. Month 3+
     User: Leadership reviews the shared KPI scorecard showing higher retention and engagement health, with credit shared across teams.
     AI: Multi-touch attribution and rollup quantify the orchestration lift.
     Feeling: Vindication — donor-centric orchestration measurably beats siloed asking.

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (10 beats) - the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Marcus RSVPs to the campus Khoury showcase via an event link.
     System: Intent signal captured and mapped to the 'computer science research' affinity.
     Motion/feedback: A new node pulses onto Marcus's journey timeline with a soft glow. (300ms)
  2. (Behind the scenes) Three teams have asks queued for Marcus this week.
     System: Conflict detection groups them into one conflict cluster and scores each for relevance and fatigue.
     Motion/feedback: Three touchpoint cards fan into a stacked conflict card on the officer view. (450ms)
  3. System evaluates Marcus's fatigue score (78, amber-red).
     System: Fatigue guardrail flags that only one ask may proceed.
     Motion/feedback: Fatigue gauge needle eases into the amber zone, which breathes slowly. (500ms)
  4. System ranks the three competing touchpoints.
     System: Khoury invite scores 92; annual-fund ask 48; athletics text 39.
     Motion/feedback: Relevance bars grow with staggered timing; the top card lifts forward. (600ms)
  5. Next-Best-Engagement generator runs.
     System: Selects the Khoury email, suppresses the annual-fund ask, defers athletics 14 days.
     Motion/feedback: The two redundant cards slide down and dim with a soft settle; the chosen card stays bright. (550ms)
  6. System checks Marcus's channel affinity (email 0.86) and timing window.
     System: Confirms email at 8:30am next morning as the receptivity peak.
     Motion/feedback: Channel chip and timing chip snap onto the action card with a gentle click. (350ms)
  7. Officer reviews the next-best-action card.
     System: Displays a one-line warm rationale explaining the suppression and timing.
     Motion/feedback: Rationale text fades in line by line beneath the card. (400ms)
  8. Officer clicks 'Approve'.
     System: The invite is scheduled; suppressed asks are logged with reasons.
     Motion/feedback: A satisfying check sweep animates across the card; calendar collision cell turns calm green. (450ms)
  9. 8:30am next day — the email sends.
     System: Single coherent invite delivered to Marcus; no other asks land.
     Motion/feedback: Timeline node advances to 'sent' with a quiet confirm pulse. (300ms)
  10. Marcus opens and engages with the invite.
     System: Positive signal captured; sentiment trend nudges upward.
     Motion/feedback: Sentiment sparkline ticks up; a small upward arrow eases into view. (400ms)

SUCCESS CRITERIA (Stage 5 audits the prototype against each of these):
  - A donor never receives more than one solicitation per fatigue-window; redundant asks are visibly suppressed with logged reasons.
  - Every next-best-engagement recommendation includes a human-readable rationale and an explicit channel + timing.
  - Conflict detection surfaces 100% of same-7-day-window collisions in the seed dataset with a one-click resolution.
  - Channel affinity predictions align with declared preference for ≥85% of donors who have one set.
  - The donor journey timeline renders all cross-team touchpoints as one coherent, legible story for every demo donor.
  - Sentiment trajectory updates and raises a care flag before a cooling donor would otherwise be re-solicited.
  - Shared KPI scorecard attributes conversions across all contributing teams rather than last-touch only.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
  Brand: Evoke Northeastern advancement context warmly without infringing official brand assets; use a deep-red accent sparingly, neutral paper-toned base, no copyrighted logos.
  Platform: web
  Accessibility: WCAG AA
  Other:
    - No verbatim donor quotes or testimonials over 80 characters in any field or rendered copy.
    - All AI features must have multi-provider fallback (Gemini primary, Claude for creative copy, graceful degradation on failure).
    - Donor data shown must be synthetic/seeded — no real PII.
    - Suppression and override decisions must always be logged and auditable for governance.
    - Motion must respect prefers-reduced-motion settings.

brief.one_line_thesis: Reframes Northeastern's advancement gap as a donor-experience problem: orchestrate every touchpoint so the donor never feels handed off.

motion_contract.encodes: Horizontal scroll with parallax depth on the active stage conveys progression through the relationship over time
Soft glow pulse marks a freshly captured high-intent signal worth acting on now
Cards fanning into a stack visualizes three separate asks colliding into one decision
Slide-down and dim communicates graceful suppression — deferred, not deleted — reducing anxiety
Staggered growth ranks competing asks so the winning ask's lead reads instantly
Eased needle position maps cumulative ask-load; slow breathing of amber/red signals caution without urgency
Lift-and-shadow rise into focus elevates the single chosen engagement as the moment of clarity
A single satisfying sweep rewards the resolution and signals decisive completion
Eased sweep length encodes affinity strength per channel
Line-by-line fade-in mimics a considered human explanation rather than a data dump
Left-to-right draw encodes trajectory over time; the direction of the final stroke reads as warming or cooling
Staggered bar growth plus counting-up numerals attributes shared credit and weights team contribution

critique.summary: Coverage is ~60% (18/30): the modal happy paths largely work and the AI plumbing (multi-provider fallback, tolerant JSON parse, VS) is correct, but the two DEPTH_FIRST_SCREENS are anemic (no suppression audit log, no override modal, no real timeline nodes, no relevance-scoring breakdown), and the edge/tail buckets fail heavily on auditability, accessibility, mobile, opt-out governance, and missing screens. Several spec-mandated states (suppression log, override-reason modal, care-flag guardrail, account context) are absent.

failed_sessions.missing_piece: No suppression audit log surface with actor/reason/timestamp entries anywhere in conflict_alert.
Override button is a no-op stub; no relevance scoring breakdown or logged override path.
No responsive/mobile layout; fixed 80px padding and horizontal ribbon break single-thumb use.
Relevance bars color-only, no ARIA labels; no prefers-reduced-motion handling for fan-out/animations.
No donor self-service preference view; confirms suppression of calls only indirectly.
Override button no-op; conflict cards lack keyboard-reachable logical Tab order/focus on let-through after resolve.
Orchestrator still 'lets one through' on red-fatigue cooling donor; no all-solicitations-blocked guardrail path.
No sessionStorage persistence; prior resolution/approval state lost on reload, no recovery view.
No account/institution context indicator anywhere in chrome.
No in-context hints/tooltips explaining fatigue gauge or conflict cards.
No opt-out/binding-suppression surfacing; intent signal can silently override standing opt-out.
No visible 'synthetic/seeded data' assurance label for non-technical demo viewer.
